outcome_classes.verdict: a checked semantic answer (Valid, Satisfied, Found, ALL, CONFLICT, Checked, ...)
outcome_classes.unknown: semantic UNKNOWN: the checker ran to completion and bounded search or proof found neither answer
outcome_classes.rejection: the input is invalid; a VEError code other than ResourceLimit
outcome_classes.budget: ResourceLimit: a deterministic public work budget or structural cap was reached
outcome_classes.operational: CheckerUnavailable: no verdict was obtained (backend missing or mismatched, crash, timeout, malformed output, or a migrated operation reached a non-authoritative engine); never a verdict, never UNKNOWN, never ResourceLimit

authorities.python: Python produces the verdict; Lean and Rust are optional cross-checks or test oracles
authorities.migrated: Lean produces the verdict; every Python entry raises AuthorityViolation (CheckerUnavailable)
authorities.lean-only: no Python implementation may exist (migration plan section 6); under python authority the operation is CheckerUnavailable

rust.role: the only search (lean-first 15b): proposes candidates and witnesses; its candidate evaluator is generator-internal and its witnesses are checked by Lean

notes: Search has no theorem; its soundness is countermodel.check's. Every candidate passes the `ve.search:check_countermodel` verdict entry before `Found` is reported (a distinguishing model is checked as a countermodel to the direction it refutes), so a migrated countermodel.check makes search CheckerUnavailable rather than bypassed.

Lean-first batch 15b: Python has no search of its own. Rust's search proposes under every authority; Lean checks every reported witness (the countermodel.check entry under Lean's authority) and its non-vacuity (`ve_metered`, `VE.Route.NonVacuity`). Rust's candidate evaluator stays generator-internal (rule 3): the batch-15b measurement (docs/lean-first/b15b) found Lean evaluation of every candidate over the bluedot search deadline.

operations.summary: A yes-or-no question read as one of the document's sentences (docs/spec/question-answering.md, Q1): Lean decides its forms, candidates, one reading, refusals and rephrasings

assurance.reason: Lean decides every outcome (VE.Question.readQuestion over E2's unchanged read; all fifteen statements of spec 5.1 proved); the case decoder is E2's and the response encoder is trusted; a reading whose fronted word was put back inside a clause is refused (VE.Question.ask), and the A0 line passes the answer frames' all-derivations gate before it is shown; no answer to the question is given (Q2)

notes: The relay ve.backends.english_lean:read_question asks the service through ve.backends.relay (not ve.backends.lean.run, so it has no lean_call_sites entry); it validates the answer's fields per status against Lean's exported contract (ve/question/codes.json, tools/question_codes.py) and the request identities, and raises the class Lean names with Lean's text.

Two readers and three evaluators (tests/test_question_differential.py): Lean's reader against an independent Python reader written from the spec over Python's own English reader (tests/question_reference.py; test code, not a product path) on every fixture and its seeded 1- and 2-fault mutants; every formula Lean reads is checked by Rust's kernel and evaluated alike by Python's evaluator, Lean's metered evaluator and Rust on seeded models. Rust has no question reader.
The budget class is the status `budget`, with the code QuestionTooLong (a size limit) or Budget (a candidate's work limit).
